citation.description: Root cause documented in ticket description and comments (measured 2026-10-27 21:35–22:00 PDT). Code in sync.py and git_outcome.py reflects the identified cause. Three hypotheses explicitly refuted with measurement evidence.

criteria.criterion: Root cause identified with evidence and the three original hypotheses distinguished: not a snapshot conflict, not a missing merge strategy, but a wall-clock timeout misreported as a conflict.

Reproduction: `merge-tree` clean + disjoint change sets + the 49 s re-hash against a 30 s bound, with the synthetic timeout string independently observed on this tracker. A direct capture of `git merge` returning 124 was NOT taken; regression tests pin the classification directly.
A timed-out sync merge is reported as a timeout naming the bound and the operation, never as "could not auto-merge … run `rebar fsck-recover`".
Local index/worktree mutations in the sync path are no longer bounded by the network `fetch` bound.
Regression tests cover: timeout → timeout report; real conflict → unchanged behaviour; timeout attempted once; the predicate's true/false cases.
